samples.summary: Non-envelope upstream bodies now discard the server's human-readable message (e.g. Nest 404 "Document not found")
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` only accepts `{error:{code:string}}`. The backend's most common failures are plain Nest exceptions — `document.service.ts:33` throws `new NotFoundException('Document not found')`, which serializes to `{message:'Document not found', error:'Not Found', statusCode:404}` (and 401/400 validation bodies similarly). Before this change those bodies were printed verbatim (the old `if (body?.error)` truthiness test matched the string `'Not Found'`, and the import paths printed `res.data` unconditionally), so the operator/agent saw the message. Now `forwardUpstreamError` throws `HTTP 404` → `{error:{code:'ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}}`, and `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}}`. The `code` is now well-shaped but all diagnostic detail from the server is dropped. Folding a `message` from the body (e.g. `typeof body.message === 'string'`) into the synthesized envelope would keep both properties.

samples.summary: `files download` can emit a misleading `HTTP 200` error message when the response is ok but carries no bytes
samples.evidence: The guard is `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`. When `res.ok` is true but `res.bytes` is missing (empty/absent body), `upstreamErrorJson(res)` falls through to the synthesized envelope and produces `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 200'}}` — a success status reported as an HTTP error. Previously the body printed was `res.data ?? {error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}`, with no misleading status. This path deserves its own code/message (e.g. EMPTY_RESPONSE) rather than reusing the status-based text.

samples.summary: `isErrorEnvelope` accepts an empty-string `code`, which is forwarded verbatim as a valid envelope
samples.evidence: `typeof (err as {code?: unknown}).code === 'string'` admits `code: ''`. A body `{error:{code:''}}` is forwarded untouched, giving consumers an envelope with no branchable code — exactly the failure mode the helper exists to prevent. `errorCode` in the same file (line 44) already guards with `code.length > 0`; the new predicate should match that.
